causes.text: China's property market faced a severe slump, with an oversupply of homes causing prices to tumble and households slipping into negative equity; officials vowed to arrest the housing downturn and boost growth, acknowledging that the real estate crisis was dragging down consumer spending and economic activity.

source_info.title: China announces measures to halt housing slump amid negative equity crisis

effects.text: BMW reported a 61% drop in third-quarter profit in 2024 as weak China sales and brake issues weighed on results; shares fell nearly 5% amid concerns about slowing demand and potential U.S. tariffs.

source_info.title: BMW profit plunges as weak China sales and brake issues hit third quarter

causal_reasoning_chain.description: China's real estate sector slumped, with an oversupply of homes causing prices to fall and households sliding into negative equity; policymakers acknowledged the crisis and sought to stabilise the market.
The property slump depressed consumer confidence and spending, reducing demand for luxury goods such as premium automobiles in China.
BMW's third-quarter 2024 profit fell 61% due partly to slumping China sales; its share price dropped about 4.8% on the day of the announcement.

rationale: China's housing crisis eroded household wealth and confidence, curbing discretionary spending on luxury items like cars. Consequently, BMW sold fewer vehicles in China, leading to a significant profit decline in the third quarter of 2024.
counterfactual_analysis: If China's real estate market had remained stable and consumer confidence high, demand for premium vehicles would have been stronger, mitigating the impact on BMW's quarterly profits.

adversarial_confounders.text: Brake system issues reported by a supplier
adversarial_confounders.impact: Mechanical problems unrelated to consumer demand also weighed on BMW's results and could independently explain part of the profit decline

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Higher rates and costs slowing global auto demand after a post-pandemic boom
details.commentary: After a period of pent-up demand, rising financing costs and broader economic uncertainty cooled consumers' appetite for big-ticket purchases like new cars. Toyota's more cautious outlook captured this economic shift, as the company prepared for slower volume growth and a less favorable pricing environment.
